key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation produces different solid-state conversion pathways in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskite stacks, so bandgap-specific control of precursor conversion is essential for all-perovskite tandems.
engineering_relevance: This work provides a solvent-free route to tune absorber bandgaps and enabled the first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell with strong efficiency and thermal stability.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Comparison of WBG Br/I mixed-halide and NBG Sn-Pb conversion behavior
Guided absorber design based on solid-state conversion mechanisms
evidence_signal: The study reports sTE absorbers spanning 1.26-1.96 eV, a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem efficiency of 19.2%, and 80% average efficiency retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: Control of vertical composition gradients and precursor thickness is critical, since incomplete FA penetration or fast lattice reorganization can lock in nonuniform absorber profiles.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
